database_summary: Small mixed-domain SQLite DB containing: a pizza-ordering dataset (menus, recipes, orders, runners, order-level extras/exclusions tables), a large urban tree inventory (trees) with neighborhood and geolocation plus an income-by-zipcode table, and separate company / funding datasets and a COVID-like statistics time series. Tables include both descriptive (dimension) tables and event/measurement tables. Join keys exist but are limited; some joins (e.g., recipes -> toppings or orders -> extras/exclusions) can multiply rows.

accepted.name: pizza_orders_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  pizza_id,
  exclusions,
  extras,
  order_time
FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders
UNION ALL
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  pizza_id,
  exclusions,
  extras,
  order_time
FROM pizza_customer_orders
WHERE order_id NOT IN (SELECT order_id FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders)
accepted.description: Normalized/cleaned one-row-per-order from pizza_clean_customer_orders and pizza_customer_orders. Prefer the cleaned table but fall back to raw if needed. Exposes canonical order_time as text, preserves ids and extras/exclusions text fields for downstream parsing. | Use for: Order-level time series (orders per day/hour/month); Join orders to pizzas, runners, extras, exclusions; Filter orders by customer_id or pizza_id

accepted.name: pizza_order_extras_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS extras_row_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(extras_count,0)) AS extras_total_count
FROM pizza_get_extras
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated extras per order from pizza_get_extras. Produces one row per order with count of extra line items and sum of extras_count. Useful to join to orders for measures of added items. | Use for: How many extras added per order; Distribution of extras per pizza or per customer

accepted.name: pizza_order_exclusions_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS exclusions_row_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(total_exclusions,0)) AS exclusions_total_reported
FROM pizza_get_exclusions
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated exclusions per order from pizza_get_exclusions. One row per order with count of exclusion line items and sum of reported total_exclusions (if provided). | Use for: How many exclusions are requested per order; Compare exclusions vs extras volumes

accepted.name: pizza_runners_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  runner_id,
  pickup_time,
  distance,
  duration,
  cancellation
FROM pizza_clean_runner_orders
accepted.description: One row per runner order event from pizza_clean_runner_orders. Keeps numeric distance and duration for analysis and preserves pickup_time. Useful as the canonical runner-order fact for performance metrics. | Use for: Average delivery distance/duration per runner; Join orders to runner performance metrics

accepted.name: trees_by_zip_income
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.idx,
  t.tree_id,
  t.tree_dbh,
  t.stump_diam,
  t.status,
  t.health,
  t.spc_latin,
  t.spc_common,
  t.address,
  t.zipcode,
  t.borocode,
  t.boroname,
  t.nta_name,
  t.state,
  t.latitude,
  t.longitude,
  i.Estimate_Total,
  i.Margin_of_Error_Total,
  i.Estimate_Median_income,
  i.Margin_of_Error_Median_income,
  i.Estimate_Mean_income,
  i.Margin_of_Error_Mean_income
FROM trees AS t
LEFT JOIN income_trees AS i
  ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
accepted.description: Denormalized view joining trees to income_trees by zipcode. One row per tree with associated income estimates for its zipcode. Useful for neighborhood-level environmental and socioeconomic analyses. | Use for: Compare tree density/health to neighborhood income; Map trees with socioeconomic attributes

accepted.name: company_funding_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  company_id,
  valuation,
  funding,
  select_investors
FROM companies_funding
accepted.description: Per-company funding and valuation measures from companies_funding. One row per company with provided funding and valuation values preserved. Useful as the canonical funding fact to join to other company tables. | Use for: Aggregate funding by year after joining to companies_dates; List investors for given company cohorts

accepted.name: covid_statistics_by_state_date
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  state,
  total_cases,
  total_deaths
FROM statistics
accepted.description: Canonical statistics time series. Preserves date, state, total_cases and total_deaths for time-series analyses and joins. Keeps raw date text as-is to allow flexible parsing later. | Use for: Compute case/death growth over time by state; Join to external population data for rates

accepted.name: pizza_names_dim
accepted.description: Canonical pizza names dimension: one row per pizza with pizza_name. Use to join to orders for human-readable labels. | Use for: Top pizzas by orders; Filter orders by pizza_name

accepted.name: pizza_toppings_dim
accepted.description: Canonical topping dimension: one row per topping providing topping_name. Useful to join exploded recipe or extras/exclusions ids to human-readable names. | Use for: Name toppings used in recipes or order extras/exclusions; Frequency of topping usage
